+// SparseCraft design point.
+// hash: 57db9c2e428dc22f   hw: e7955f4f5e66a51e   sw: f6342c9ddfeb3619
+//
+// The SPARSECRAFT lines below are SOFTWARE-side: tiling and the
+// sparsity pattern. They are compiler
+// defines, not Chisel parameters, so they live in comments -- but the harness
+// parses them back out, so they must be kept and kept well-formed.
+// SPARSECRAFT workload = dnn512
+// SPARSECRAFT dense_mode = 0
+//
+// ============================ ITERATION 4 ============================
+// meshRows/meshColumns 16 -> 32 (L2 geometry). plan_id = GEOM32, step 1 of 2.
+//
+// WHY GEOMETRY AND NOT MORE SPARSITY RTL -- three measurements, not a guess:
+//
+// (1) T-A is SATURATED. MAC_GATED_TOTAL = 7,864,320 and
+//     macs_issued - macs_useful = 8,388,608 - 524,288 = 7,864,320. Identical.
+//     Every zero-operand multiply in the array is already gated; there is no
+//     ungated zero left to find. Iteration 2 priced the entire MAC term at
+//     95.673 -> 93.550 uJ = 2.12 uJ for 7.86M gated MACs (0.27 pJ each), so
+//     even a perfect further gate is worth <0.3 uJ of today's 30.1 uJ.
+//     PE.scala already holds BOTH multiplier inputs and the accumulate input.
+//
+// (2) T-B CANNOT REMOVE A CYCLE IN THIS TREE, and its energy is invisible.
+//     Verified by reading the harness-owned integration, not assumed:
+//       - ScratchpadBank drives `io.sc_zbu_skip`, and NOTHING in the generator
+//         reads that port. There is no ExecuteController query.
+//       - `skip` only gates `mem.read(raddr, ren && !sc_skip)` and muxes a
+//         hard zero into the response queue. `io.read.req.ready` and
+//         `q.io.enq.valid := RegNext(ren)` are untouched, so issue rate,
+//         preload and compute passes are all unchanged by construction.
+//       - CounterFile exposes ONE SparseCraft external counter,
+//         MAC_GATED_TOTAL = 8. There is no ZBU event id, so suppressed SRAM
+//         reads cannot reach the counter-driven energy model.
+//     Enabling it therefore buys a measurable zero and pays ~16K bitmap flops
+//     (4 banks x 4,096 rows) of real area: a strictly dominated point. Left at
+//     0 for the second iteration running, now on read evidence rather than
+//     inference.
+//
+// (3) TIME IS CYCLES HERE. area_source reports
+//     T3_nangate45_logic+fakeram45_macros_TIMING_UNUSABLE, and the measured
+//     numbers close on a FIXED period: 30.111 uJ / 0.1895 W = 158.9 us over
+//     79,433 cycles = 2.000 ns exactly. So an Fmax-motivated move (e.g.
+//     re-pipelining the T-A comparator off the MAC critical path) cannot be
+//     scored, and cycles are the only handle on the time axis.
+//
+// WHAT THE CYCLES ARE ACTUALLY DOING. exe_active = 0.8953 of 79,433 = 71,116
+// compute-state cycles over 2,048 issued tile-ops = 34.7 cyc/tile-op, i.e.
+// 2 x DIM + epsilon. The preload pass costs DIM cycles per tile-op whatever
+// DIM is, so HALF the cycle budget is weight-shift, not arithmetic. That term
+// amortises against DIM, and nothing in PE.scala or the ZBU touches it.
+//
+// THE BOUND IS HARD, NOT ESTIMATED. A 512x512 A has only 16x16 = 256 blocks of
+// 32x32 and X has 2 column blocks, so there are at most 16*16*2 = 512 tile-ops
+// at DIM=32, versus the 2,048 issued at DIM=16. Even if coarser blocking made
+// EVERY 32x32 block nonzero -- the worst case, block-skip reduced to nothing --
+//     cycles <= 512 * (2*32) = 32,768   vs   2,048 * (2*16) = 65,536
+// so this is at least a 2x cycle reduction with no assumption about the
+// matrix's structure. Real SuiteSparse clustering should beat that.
+//
+// WHAT IS BEING SPENT: area. 1,024 PEs instead of 256. The gate delta priced
+// PE logic at (4,107,785-4,034,991)/256 = 284 um2 per PE of T-A alone, and a
+// whole INT8 PE with a 32b accumulate is several times that, so expect order
+// +25% area. Energy should still IMPROVE, because at a fixed 2 ns period the
+// 0.19 W is dominated by a cycles-proportional term (DMA is now only 327,680
+// bytes and the MAC term is ~2.4 uJ) -- halving cycles halves that.
+//
+// COUPLING TO T-A, which is why this is not a bare knob turn: a 32x32 block is
+// all-zero far less often than a 16x16 one, so coarsening the geometry pushes
+// MORE zeros past the software block-skip and INTO the array. macs_issued will
+// rise even as cycles fall. That surviving population is exactly what T-A
+// eats, and T-A is on and saturated -- the geometry move is only safe on the
+// energy axis BECAUSE the zero-gated MAC is already there to absorb it.
+// Expect MAC_GATED_TOTAL to rise while energy still falls.
+//
+// STEP 2 OF plan_id = GEOM32 (next iteration, if area is what gets scored
+// against this): right-size sp_capacity. At DIM=32 the resident set is
+// X 1,024 rows + k_chunk*DIM = 512 rows of A + 1,024 rows of B = 2,560 rows of
+// the 8,192 that 256 KB provides at a 32 B row -- 3.2x over-provisioned. 128 KB
+// still holds it with 1.6x headroom and hands back SRAM macro area to pay for
+// the mesh. Deliberately NOT bundled here: bundling it would make the area
+// number unattributable between mesh growth and SRAM shrink.
+// =====================================================================
+//
+// The Gemmini instruction schedule (Sec 9o's software co-design levers). They
+// reach the build as -DSPMM_KCHUNK / -DSPMM_B_BLOCKS (nodes.py), but they were
+// NOT emitted here, so nothing wrote them into the tree and read_design_state
+// could not read them back: every proposal silently reverted to the defaults
+// the moment the state was re-parsed. Measured 2026-09-20 -- a run launched
+// with k_chunk=64 reported `[SW] k_chunk 64 -> 16` and reused the baseline's
+// sw_hash, i.e. the whole software half of co-design was inert, for the agent
+// and the CLI alike.
+//
+// x_resident 0 -> 1 (iteration 3) MEASURED, and it worked: RDMA_BYTES_REC
+// 3,080,192 -> 196,608 B (15.7x), cycles 106,650 -> 79,433, energy
+// 93.550 -> 30.111 uJ (3.1x), exe_active 0.39 -> 0.90. It converted a
+// scratchpad-wait-bound design into a compute-bound one, which is what makes
+// L2 geometry the correct next lever. Held at 1; capacity re-checked for
+// DIM=32 above.
+// SPARSECRAFT k_chunk = 16
+// SPARSECRAFT b_blocks = 0
+// SPARSECRAFT x_resident = 1
+// The four below are RTL-microarchitecture parameters. They are markers, NOT
+// GemminiArrayConfig fields, until Phase 3 adds the corresponding Chisel
+// parameters -- emitting them as `.copy(gate_enable = ...)` before the field
+// exists makes elaboration fail with a Scala type error.
+//
+// gate_enable 0 -> 1 (iteration 2): MAC_GATED_TOTAL measured 7,864,320 of
+// 8,388,608 issued MACs, i.e. 93.75% of every multiply the array performed had
+// a zero streaming operand. T-A turns that into quiet cycles. Cycles are
+// unchanged by construction; this buys the energy axis and spends a little
+// area and Fmax on the comparator and the two isolation muxes in PE.scala.
+// Kept ON at iteration 4, and now load-bearing: see the COUPLING note above.
+// PE.scala is untouched this iteration -- it is saturated (finding (1)).
+// SPARSECRAFT gate_enable = 1
+//
+// zbu_enable stays 0. See finding (2) above: the skip output is unconsumed,
+// there is no ZBU counter event, and the bitmap is pure area. Revisit only if
+// the harness wires an ExecuteController query and a ZBU event id, at which
+// point granule_size becomes a real search axis; until then it is not one.
+// granule_size is left at 16, which still divides the new DIM=32 and so
+// remains T0-legal.
+// SPARSECRAFT zbu_enable = 0
+// SPARSECRAFT granule_size = 16
+// SPARSECRAFT zbu_operand = A
+package gemmini
+
+import chisel3._
+
+object SparseCraftParams {
+  val config = GemminiConfigs.defaultConfig.copy(
+    // --- L2 PE array geometry ---
+    // 16 -> 32. Square and a power of 2: meshRows*tileRows == 32 ==
+    // meshColumns*tileColumns. The preload pass is DIM cycles per tile-op
+    // regardless of DIM, and it is half of today's 34.7 cyc/tile-op, so it
+    // only amortises by making the tile-op bigger.
+    meshRows    = 32,
+    meshColumns = 32,
+    tileRows    = 1,
+    tileColumns = 1,
+    dataflow    = Dataflow.WS,
+
+    // --- L3 scratchpad / accumulator ---
+    // Unchanged, and re-checked against the new DIM rather than assumed:
+    //   spad rows/bank = 256 KB / 4 banks / (32 B row) = 2,048 -- a power of 2
+    //                    and a multiple of DIM=32. Resident set 2,560 of 8,192.
+    //   acc  rows/bank =  64 KB / 2 banks / (128 B row) = 256 -- power of 2,
+    //                    multiple of 32. Output tile 32x64xint32 = 8 KB.

+    acc_capacity    = CapacityInKilobytes(64),
+    sp_banks        = 4,
+    acc_banks       = 2,
+    spad_read_delay = 4,
+    acc_latency     = 2,
+

+// See README.md for license details.
+package gemmini
+
+import chisel3._
+import chisel3.util._
+
+/** Zero-Bitmap Unit (ZBU) -- T-B: zero-granule skipping.
+  *
+  * ==== INTERFACE -- THIS PORT LIST IS A CONTRACT ====
+  *
+  * Scratchpad.scala is harness-owned and instantiates this module verbatim.
+  * It will not adapt to a changed port list, so renaming or re-typing a port
+  * fails elaboration. Everything INSIDE the module is yours.
+  *
+  *   n   rows in the bank -- one bitmap bit per row
+  *   w   row width in bits
+  *
+  *   io.write_fire  Input  Bool       a write is landing this cycle
+  *   io.write_addr  Input  UInt       its row
+  *   io.write_data  Input  UInt(w.W)  its data
+  *   io.write_full  Input  Bool       the write covers the WHOLE row
+  *   io.read_addr   Input  UInt       the row being read this cycle
+  *   io.read_en     Input  Bool       a read is being issued this cycle
+  *   io.skip        Output Bool       this read may be skipped: row is zero
+  *
+  * ==== SEMANTICS THE HARNESS RELIES ON ====
+  *
+  *  - `skip` may be high ONLY when the row is KNOWN to be entirely zero.
+  *    Skipping a zero row is bit-exact: the scratchpad returns a hard zero
+  *    instead of reading it, which is the same value. A WRONGLY set bit
+  *    silently corrupts the result and N41 will fail the iteration.
+  *  - A partial (masked) write must CLEAR the bit -- the row is then partly
+  *    unknown. A cleared bit is always safe, so conservative is correct.
+  *
+  * ==== WHAT TO TRY ====
+  *
+  * The seed tracks one bit per row at granule = DIM. Finer granularity finds
+  * more zeros but costs more bitmap state; tracking the B operand as well as A
+  * catches a different population; remembering a count rather than a flag lets
+  * you skip partially.
+  */
+class SparseCraftZBU(n: Int, w: Int) extends Module {
+  val io = IO(new Bundle {
+    val write_fire = Input(Bool())
+    val write_addr = Input(UInt(log2Ceil(n).W))
+    val write_data = Input(UInt(w.W))
+    val write_full = Input(Bool())
+    val read_addr  = Input(UInt(log2Ceil(n).W))
+    val read_en    = Input(Bool())
+    val skip       = Output(Bool())
+  })
+
+  // One bit per row. At granule_size = DIM a row IS a granule.
+  val bitmap = RegInit(VecInit(Seq.fill(n)(false.B)))
+
+  // Set only on a FULL-WIDTH zero write; any masked write clears it.
+  when (io.write_fire) {
+    bitmap(io.write_addr) := io.write_full && (io.write_data === 0.U)
+  }
+
+  io.skip := bitmap(io.read_addr) && io.read_en
+}
